description: Bbuilding Groundtruth: a 3D Mars orbital atlas and EVA planner for the Martian Map challenge. Real NASA data, a Cesium globe, A* rover routing, a Mars24 sun model. Working across systems, data and AI, and likes hard-to-fake engines under clean interfaces.
summary: Groundtruth is a Mars orbital atlas with an EVA planner that works anywhere on the surface, built for the Interplanetary Survival Guide: Martian Map challenge. A 3D Cesium globe layers real NASA data — Mars Trek 232 m/px imagery, HiRISE 1 m detail at Gale Crater, a 200 m MOLA/HRSC elevation model — under a real-time Mars24 sun model. Press EVA anywhere and it fetches local terrain, builds an A* rover network, and generates objectives; compare Fastest, Safest and Most Science plans against power, radiation dose and slope, then run the traverse leg by leg for a graded field log. It matters because a Marswalk is won or lost in planning: Groundtruth turns scattered mission data into one honest, testable plan, so astronauts can explore further while staying safe — and do new science on the way.
details:
Groundtruth is a Mars orbital atlas with an EVA planner that works anywhere on the surface. It opens on a 3D Cesium globe of Mars layered with real mission data: Mars Trek 232 m/px imagery, a 200 m MOLA/HRSC elevation model, HiRISE 1 m detail at Gale Crater, the USGS geologic map, landing sites, rover traverses and 1,794 searchable named features, all lit by a real-time Mars24 sun model with a moving day/night terminator.

Press EVA anywhere — pick a point, search a feature, or enter coordinates — and Groundtruth fetches the local terrain window, builds an A* rover network over it, and generates terrain-grounded objectives. For each leg you compare three plans — Fastest, Safest, Most science — against power, radiation dose (0.026 mSv/h baseline, 0.25 mSv EVA rule), slope (25° hard no-go), solar-event multipliers and loadout mass, then run the traverse leg by leg for a graded field log. Gale Crater is the showcase: real Vera Rubin Ridge and Hematite Hotspot objectives, sample stops and actual Curiosity POV imagery; everywhere else is clearly labelled as 200 m reconnaissance.

It is built with Vite, React 19, TypeScript, CesiumJS, Leaflet, geotiff.js and Tailwind CSS, and deployed on GitHub Pages. The benefit is focus: today a Marswalk planner must stitch together a dozen mission archives by hand. Groundtruth puts them in one testable plan, and it is honest about what it does not know — data grade is always visible, and the energy, dose and thermal numbers are labelled planning models, not measured telemetry. The intended impact is practical: safer EVAs, more science per outing, and a tool a crew could actually rehearse with. The creative leap is EVA anywhere — not a scripted tour of one crater, but a planner that works at any point on Mars, with consequences for every choice you make.
